description: BRTDP (*bounded RTDP*) keeps a lower bound `L` and an upper bound `U` on `V*`, the optimal expected cost of each state. `L` comes from an admissible heuristic and `U` from a finite upper heuristic, and `L ≤ V* ≤ U` holds at all times. Trials follow the action that is greedy on `L` and sample each successor by its probability times its gap `U − L`. The run stops when `U − L ≤ ε` at the start state, and the policy is greedy on `U`. It is *anytime*: you can stop it early and still know how far the policy can be from optimal.

papers.authors: H. Brendan McMahan, Maxim Likhachev, Geoffrey J. Gordon
papers.title: Bounded real-time dynamic programming: RTDP with monotone upper bounds and performance guarantees
